title: A Neutral Atom-Based Hybrid Classical-Quantum Approach for the Entanglement Routing Problem
authors: M. Yassine Naghmouchi, Quentin Ma, Agathe Blaise, René Veyland, Wesley Coelho
abstract: Efficient end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum information networks requires routing under limited resources and fidelity constraints. We study entanglement routing as a fidelity-constrained unsplittable multicommodity flow problem that maximizes the number of admitted requests. As a proof of concept, we integrate neutral-atom quantum optimization into a hybrid classical--quantum column-generation framework. A classical restricted master problem selects routes, while a pricing problem generates fidelity-feasible paths. We formulate this NP-hard constrained shortest-path pricing problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and address it with hardware-aware register embedding and instance-driven pulse shaping. To our knowledge, this is the first study of neutral-atom quantum optimization as a pricing oracle for fidelity-constrained entanglement routing. On small benchmark instances evaluated with neutral-atom processor emulators, the method, combined with warm-start and post-processing, achieves an optimality gap below 1% across all tested sizes; the selected simulated-annealing route-generation baseline exhibits gaps of up to 6%. These results indicate that the generated bitstrings can provide useful candidate routes for classical refinement within column generation. This proof of concept does not establish quantum utility or scalability; further evaluation on larger instances, against stronger classical baselines, and on quantum hardware is needed.
summary: This work tackles the complex, NP-hard problem of routing entanglement in quantum networks under fidelity constraints. It proposes a novel hybrid framework that uses neutral-atom quantum processors to solve the path-finding subproblem within a column generation algorithm. The results demonstrate that this quantum integration yields highly accurate candidate routes for classical refinement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the Entanglement Routing in Quantum Networks (ERQN) problem, which is formulated as a fidelity-constrained unsplittable multicommodity flow problem.
main_result: The hybrid classical-quantum approach achieved an optimality gap below 1% on tested benchmarks, significantly outperforming classical baselines when combined with warm-start and post-processing.
method: A hybrid classical-quantum column generation framework is used, where the NP-hard pricing subproblem is formulated as a QUBO and solved using a neutral-atom quantum optimization routine.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a neutral atom quantum processor utilizing Rydberg interactions. The problem is modeled using graph theory for network flow, constrained by fidelity decay factors.
key_observables: Optimality gap relative to the exact ILP solution, number of admitted entanglement requests, and mean column-generation iterations.
important_parameters: Link capacity ($C_e$), per-hop fidelity decay ($\pi_e$), and minimum required end-to-end fidelity ($F_k$).
main_assumptions: The study assumes a deterministic, per-round routing decision, simplifying the model by ignoring stochastic link availability, waiting times, or finite entanglement lifetimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum network architecture and show the mean optimality gap and mean column-generation iterations versus network size for various reinforcement strategies (warm-start, post-processing).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the ERQN problem, formulates it as a column generation problem, and proposes integrating a neutral-atom quantum solver (mapping to QUBO) as the pricing oracle, followed by benchmarking against classical methods.
why_interesting: It directly applies advanced quantum hardware capabilities (neutral atoms) to solve a critical, resource-intensive problem in quantum networking (entanglement routing), bridging quantum computation with quantum information theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Quantum network architecture for entanglement routing. A centralized controller monitors stochastic link availability and computes routing decisions each generation round via classical control links. The local segment shows Alice (source) and Bob (destination) connected through three intermediate repeaters R1, R2, R3 over lossy quantum links. The orange mesh illustrates the quantum backbone over which E2E entanglement is established via entanglement swapping at intermediate repeaters.

FIG. 2: Overall workflow of the proposed hybrid classical–quantum column-generation method. Classical computation is used for solving the RMP and the final restricted ILP, while the pricing phase is handled through a quantum-assisted optimization routine.

FIG. 3: Example of a pulse generated by the proposed instance-driven pulse shaping procedure. Top: global Rabi amplitude Ω(t) controls quantum mixing. Middle: global detuning δg(t) defines the classical energy landscape. Bottom: local detuning contribution δDMM(t) used to encode the diagonal QUBO coefficients. The sequence starts from a strongly negative detuning to prepare the initial state and progressively transitions toward a problem-dominated Hamiltonian.

FIG. 4: Mean column-generation iterations vs. network size N on Topology 1 (20 instances per size N). (a) No reinforcement: CG-SA is flat at 2, whereas CG-Q stabilizes around 2.4. (b) Warm-start only: both methods grow together from ∼1.5 to 2.0–2.1. (c) Post-processing only: profiles are virtually identical to the base case. (d) Warm-start + post-processing: the trend closely matches the WS-only case.

FIG. 5: Mean column-generation iterations vs. network size N on Topology 2 (20 instances per size N). (a) No reinforcement: CG-SA remains at 2, whereas CG-Q rises to 3.7 at N=12. (b) Warm-start only: both methods grow steeply to 3.3–3.4. (c) Post-processing only: profiles remain close to the base case. (d) Warm-start + post-processing: the trend closely matches the WS-only case.
